summary: Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at Technical University of Berlin, University of Manchester, and University of Cambridge, where he earned his Ph.D. in 1929. He was a lecturer and fellow at Trinity College (1929–1947) and professor of philosophy at Cambridge (1930–1947).
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He later served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.
Luigi Suali worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi, later holding a post at the University of Pavia from around 1907 to 1951.

Luis O. Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned degrees at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale under Stanley Insler, and Michigan. He held professorships and chairmanships at Michigan (1976–2008) and was Academic Director at Mangalam Research Center (2010–2017).

Luise Hercus worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at St Anne's College and the Australian National University, served as tutor and lecturer at St Anne's (1948–1954), research fellow at Adelaide (1965–1969), and held posts at ANU in 1969 and 1991.
Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He earned a graduate degree at Sherubtse College, an LL.B at Government Law College, Mumbai, and an LL.M at the University of Edinburgh.

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery and studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He lectured at the University of Oslo (1967) and founded Menri Monastery, serving as its abbot from 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lutz Bieg is a Sinologist who completed his doctorate at Heidelberg University and his habilitation at Free University of Berlin. From 1989 to 2008, he was professor of Chinese studies, modern Chinese literature, and Chinese philosophy at the University of Cologne.
Lynn Struve is a historian and Sinologist. She studied at the University of Washington and the University of Michigan, and held a post at Indiana University from around 1977 to 2010.

Lynn Thomas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned degrees at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford (D.Phil. 1987), and served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Etienne Marc Quatremère. He held the Chair of Tibetan at INALCO (1865), lectured at Collège de France (1869–1872), and was a librarian at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872).

Léon Vandermeersch was a Sinologist and philosopher who studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held posts at Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and directed the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1989–1993).

Lê Mạnh Thát works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history. He earned his BA at Saigon University and his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding a post at Vạn Hạnh University from around 1974 to 1975.

M. A. Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and as Professor of Sanskrit and Professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970 and 1983).
M. Athar Ali was a historian who studied at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1948 to 1961 and served as a historian there from around 1953 to 1990.
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University by 1969 and held a post there (attested 1967).

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian who studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and UCL under Ernest Arthur Gardner and others. He served at the University of Mysore (attested 1910, 1939) and headed the department at Maharaja's College (1932).

M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She was a fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990), professor at King's College London (1990–2014), and held posts at UCL and Newnham College.

M. N. Srinivas was an Indologist and sociologist who studied under M. H. Krishna, G. S. Ghurye, and at Oxford. He taught at Baroda (1951–1959), Delhi (1959), and helped found and chair the Institute for Social and Economic Change (1972–1979).
